reasoning: Most failures are already covered by the skill's answer-granularity and evidence-check rules, so repeating them would not address a real gap. The person-name rule can be made less rigid: choose the form best supported by the clue-matching evidence instead of automatically preferring a full or formal name.

edits.target: For a person, use an explicitly supported full personal name rather than a familiar nickname when the full name is relevant, and preserve honorifics that are part of the context-supported conventional name, especially when the clue cues them.
edits.content: For a person, use the name form most directly supported by the clue-matching context rather than mechanically preferring a formal or legal expansion over a familiar public name. Use a full personal name when the clue or its closest matching evidence calls for it; otherwise preserve the conventional public form. Retain honorifics when they are part of the context-supported conventional name or are cued by the clue.
